findings.title: queue:work and websockets:serve marked DOWN in observability dashboard (dev env)
findings.evidence: C-08-observability.png — both badges DOWN with 'Aucun signal'; 0 événements dispatched (24h). Observability is correctly REPORTING the state — the bug is the absence of the workers in this local environment, not a code defect.
findings.impact: In local dev this is expected if `php artisan queue:work` and `npx ws` are not running. The risk is that the same DOWN state in production would mask broadcast/sync features without louder alerting beyond an admin-only banner.
findings.recommendation: Production runbook check: confirm supervisord/systemd starts queue + websockets workers. Optionally add an alerting hook from the observability dashboard so 'DOWN' triggers ops paging (not just an admin banner).
findings.fix_blocked_reason: Operational/infrastructure concern, not a code defect. Re-classified from P0 to P2 (advisor feedback): the dashboard is already surfacing the truth; production posture is unverified by this audit.

findings.title: /admin (root) returns Vue SPA 404 even when authenticated
findings.evidence: C-04-admin-root.png — header shows 'Compte' (= logged in) but body renders Vue 404. /admin/dashboard (C-04b) works.
findings.impact: Any URL truncation or bookmark to /admin sends an authenticated admin to 404 with no redirect. Poor UX, breaks discoverability.
findings.recommendation: Add `{ path: '/admin', redirect: { name: 'admin.dashboard' } }` in resources/js/router/index.js (same pattern already used for /kds → admin.kitchen-display-system).
findings.fix_blocked_reason: Safe ~3 LOC fix but requires verifying the dashboard route NAME (some V1 builds use admin.dashboard, others admin.home). Deferred to round 2 to do alongside dashboard NAME audit.

findings.title: Items page STATUT and Stock-rupture dashboard DISPONIBILITÉ disagree for Chicken Burger
findings.evidence: C-09c-p3.png — /admin/items shows Chicken Burger STATUT 'Actif', DISPONIBILITÉ action 'Marquer Indisponible', and the header card 'INDISPONIBLES: 0'. C-10/C-10b — /admin/stock/rupture shows Chicken Burger badge 'RUPTURE'. The two admin surfaces give the operator contradictory information.
findings.impact: If an admin opens /admin/items first, they conclude Chicken Burger is available. If they open /admin/stock/rupture, they see it's out. The header card 'INDISPONIBLES: 0' is plain wrong — at least Chicken Burger is in rupture state. Operator decisions (re-stock, customer info) depend on which surface they look at — high risk of customer-facing miscommunication.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) merge STATUT and DISPONIBILITÉ into a single source of truth in /admin/items, or (b) add an explicit DISPONIBILITÉ badge column showing 'EN STOCK' / 'RUPTURE' next to STATUT. Update the header card INDISPONIBLES counter to query the same flag the rupture dashboard uses.
findings.fix_blocked_reason: Investigative — needs to confirm which DB column / API endpoint each surface reads, and align them. Likely 'is_active' (statut) vs 'availability' (disponibilité) drift.

findings.title: /admin/items header tile 'ACTIFS' shows per-page count, not global active count
findings.evidence: C-09-items-page1.png shows tile 'ACTIFS 10' (page 1 has 10 actif items). C-09c-p5.png shows 'ACTIFS 5' (page 5 has 5 items). Tile is page-dependent, label suggests global count.
findings.impact: Misleading dashboard KPI. Decision-makers reading 'Actifs: 10' would conclude only 10 of 45 products are active, while in reality all 45 are 'Actif'.
findings.recommendation: Compute Actifs count from a separate API call against the global items table, not from currentPage.items.filter.
